title: IES Profiles: From File Rows to Runtime Sampling
abstract: How an IES file becomes an absolute-candela texture, how that texture is sampled, and how the result drives source scaling and light meters.
imageAlt: IES file rows parsed into angular candela data and resampled into a texture
lede: An IES profile stores candela samples at measured vertical and horizontal angles. The runtime path parses those rows into an angle-indexed table, resamples the table into a 257 × 257 R32F texture, and looks up directional candela from the light-to-camera direction.

sections.heading: Read the file row by row
paragraphs: LM-63 is token-based, so a long list may wrap across physical lines. Conceptually, the data appears in this order: format and metadata, tilt data, photometric fields, angle arrays, then candela rows.

codeBlocks.code:
IESNA:LM-63-2002
[keywords and test metadata]
TILT=NONE
lamps lumensPerLamp candelaMultiplier verticalCount horizontalCount photometricType unitType width length height
ballastFactor futureUse inputWatts
[vertical angles]
[horizontal angles]
[candela values for horizontal plane 0]
[candela values for horizontal plane 1]
...

rows: Test, manufacturer, catalog, and luminaire metadata.
No correction, an included correction table, or an external tilt file.
Lamp count, lumens per lamp, candela multiplier, angle counts, photometric type, units, and emitter dimensions.
Ballast factor, reserved value, and input watts.
verticalCount samples, normally covering part or all of 0°–180°.
horizontalCount C-planes covering the stored symmetry range.
One row per horizontal plane, with verticalCount intensity samples.

sections.heading: Load an angle-indexed candela table
paragraphs: Keep the source angles because their spacing may be irregular. Store candela in horizontal-major order so candela[p × verticalCount + a] addresses horizontal plane p and vertical angle a. Reconstruct any symmetry before texture creation.

equations.label: Absolute candela
equations.expression: I_abs(θ, φ) = I_IES(θ, φ) × M_cd × F_ballast
terms: I_IES is the source-table sample, M_cd is the candela multiplier, and F_ballast is the ballast factor.
Lumens per Lamp is parsed but not used in this calculation.

sections.heading: Recreate the profile as a 2D texture
paragraphs: Create a 257 × 257 R32F texture. Each texel stores absolute candela for one vertical angle and one horizontal C-plane angle. The duplicated horizontal endpoint closes the 0°/360° seam.

equations.label: Texture coordinates
terms: θ = 180°u is the vertical angle from 0° to 180°.
φ = 360°v is the horizontal angle from 0° to 360°.

equations.label: Source-table interpolation
terms: I00, I10, I01, and I11 are the four surrounding source samples.

sections.heading: Sample directional candela at runtime
paragraphs: Convert the light-to-camera direction into the light's photometric basis. F, U, and R are the light forward, up, and right directions.

equations.label: Light-to-camera direction
terms: d is a normalized world-space direction.

equations.label: Vertical lookup
equations.expression: θ = arccos(clamp(F · d, −1, 1)),  u = θ / π
terms: u maps the forward angle from 0 to 1.

equations.label: Horizontal C-plane lookup
equations.expression: C0 = −U,  C90 = −R,  φ = atan2(d · C90, d · C0),  v = mod(φ + 2π, 2π) / 2π
terms: v wraps the azimuth into the 0–1 range.

equations.label: Directional intensity
terms: The texture lookup uses bilinear filtering and returns absolute candela.

sections.heading: Scale the visible source without changing its area
paragraphs: Directional candela can enlarge the screen-space glare source. This affects only its visible axes; the physical emitter area remains unchanged. Each screen-space axis is clamped to at least 1.5 pixels.

equations.label: Glare scale
terms: α is ScalingAreaAlpha. Apply the optional limit S = min(S, S_max).
R_scaled = S R_screen and U_scaled = S U_screen.

technicalTables.caption: w and h are half-extents in centimetres; r is the radius. The factor 10⁻⁴ converts cm² to m².

sections.heading: Compute brightness and directional meter values
paragraphs: The brightness meter converts candela to luminance using projected emitter area. The directional meter keeps the sampled candela. Both apply the emitter mask M and depth visibility V_d, then keep the maximum value where lights overlap.

equations.label: Projected area
terms: A is the physical emitter area and c is the viewing-angle cosine.

equations.label: Brightness meter luminance
equations.expression: L = I_dir / max(Ac, 10⁻⁶) when c > 10⁻⁴; otherwise L = I_ref / A
terms: I_ref = I(0°, 0°). L is measured in cd/m².
For light color C, L_RGB = LC and L_meter = max(L_r, L_g, L_b).
L_output = L_meter × M × V_d; L_final = max_i(L_output,i); test L_final > L_threshold.

equations.label: Directional meter
equations.expression: I_meter = I_dir × M × V_d,  I_final = max_i(I_meter,i)
terms: I_final is measured in cd; test I_final > I_threshold.

callouts.title: Current intensity path
callouts.text: The implementation samples absolute IES candela directly. It does not multiply the result by Unreal Engine light intensity.

references.label: Illuminating Engineering Society: ANSI/IES LM-63 standard listing
Epic Games: Using IES Light Profiles

closing: The pipeline is direct: parse angles and candela, apply the file multipliers, resample absolute candela into a 2D texture, and recover directional intensity with the light's runtime basis.
